records.title: Female carriers of X-linked inherited retinal diseases - Genetics, diagnosis, and potential therapies.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Female carriers of X-linked inherited retinal diseases - Genetics, diagnosis, and potential therapies.
content.abstract: Inherited retinal diseases (IRDs) are a group of heterogeneous conditions that cause progressive vision loss, typically due to monogenic mutations. Female carriers of X-linked IRDs have a single copy of the disease-causing gene, and therefore, may exhibit variable clinical signs that vary from near normal retina to severe disease and vision loss. The relationships between individual genetic mutations and disease severity in X-linked carriers requires further study. This review summarises the current literature surrounding the spectrum of disease seen in female carriers of choroideremia and X-linked retinitis pigmentosa. Various classification systems are contrasted to accurately grade retinal disease. Furthermore, genetic mechanisms at the early embryonic stage are explored to potentially explain the variability of disease seen in female carriers. Future research in this area will provide insight into the association between genotype and retinal phenotypes of female carriers, which will guide in the management of these patients. This review acknowledges the importance of identifying which patients may be at high risk of developing severe symptoms, and therefore should be considered for emerging treatments, such as retinal gene therapy.

records.title: Clinical features of endophthalmitis clusters after cataract surgery and practical recommendations to mitigate risk: systematic review.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Clinical features of endophthalmitis clusters after cataract surgery and practical recommendations to mitigate risk: systematic review.
content.abstract: Intraocular transmission of exogenous pathogens in cataract surgery can lead to endophthalmitis. This review evaluates the features of endophthalmitis clusters secondary to pathogen transmission in cataract surgery. Articles reporting on pathogen transmission in cataract surgery were identified via searches of Ovid MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane CENTRAL, and a total of 268 eyes from 24 studies were included. The most common source of infectious transmission was attributed to a contaminated intraocular solution (ie, irrigation solution, viscoelastic, or diluted antibiotic; n = 10). Visual acuity at presentation with infectious features was 1.89 logMAR (range: 1.35 to 2.58; ∼counting fingers) and 1.33 logMAR (range: 0.04 to 3.00; Snellen: ∼20/430) at last follow-up. Patients with diabetes had worse outcomes compared with patients without diabetes. The most frequently isolated pathogen from the infectious sources was Pseudomonas sp. (50.0%). This review highlights the various routes of pathogen transmission during cataract surgery and summarizes recommendations for the detection, prevention, and management of endophthalmitis clusters.

records.title: Genome-Wide Association Study of Age-Related Macular Degeneration Reveals 2 New Loci Implying Shared Genetic Components with Central Serous Chorioretinopathy.

content.title: Genome-Wide Association Study of Age-Related Macular Degeneration Reveals 2 New Loci Implying Shared Genetic Components with Central Serous Chorioretinopathy.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate the genetic architecture of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in a Japanese population.

Design

Genome-wide association study (GWAS).

Participants

Three thousand seven hundred seventy-two patients with AMD and 16 770 control participants from the Japanese population were enrolled in the association analyses.

Methods

We conducted a meta-analysis of 2 independent GWASs that included a total of 2663 patients with AMD and 9471 control participants using the imputation reference panel for genotype imputation specified for the Japanese population (n = 3541). A replication study was performed using an independent set of 1109 patients with AMD and 7299 control participants.

Main outcome measures

Associations of genetic variants with AMD.

Results

A meta-analysis of the 2 GWASs identified 6 loci significantly associated with AMD (P < 5.0 × 10-8). Of these loci, 4 were known to be associated with AMD (CFH, C2/FB, TNFRSF10A, and ARMS2), and 2 were novel (rs4147157 near WBP1L and rs76228488 near GATA5). The newly identified associations were confirmed in a replication study (P < 0.01). After the meta-analysis of all datasets, we observed strong associations in these loci (P = 1.88 × 10-12 and P = 1.35 × 10-9 for meta-analysis for rs4147157 and rs76228488, respectively). When we looked up the associations in the reported central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC) GWAS conducted in the Japanese population, both loci were associated significantly with CSC (P = 4.86 × 10-3 and P = 4.28 × 10-3 for rs4147157 and rs76228488, respectively). We performed a genetic colocalization analysis for these loci and estimated that the posterior probabilities of shared causal variants between AMD and CSC were 0.39 and 0.60 for WBP1L and GATA5, respectively. Genetic correlation analysis focusing on the epidemiologically suggested clinical risk factors implicated shared polygenic architecture between AMD and smoking cessation (rg [the measure of genetic correlation] = -0.33; P = 0.01; false discovery rate, 0.099).

Conclusions

Our findings imply shared genetic components conferring the risk of both AMD and CSC.

records.title: Myocilin misfolding and glaucoma: A 20-year update.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Myocilin misfolding and glaucoma: A 20-year update.
content.abstract: Mutations in the gene MYOC account for approximately 5% of cases of primary open angle glaucoma (POAG). MYOC encodes for the protein myocilin, a multimeric secreted glycoprotein composed of N-terminal coiled-coil (CC) and leucine zipper (LZ) domains that are connected via a disordered linker to a 30 kDa olfactomedin (OLF) domain. More than 90% of glaucoma-causing mutations are localized to the OLF domain. While myocilin is expressed in numerous tissues, mutant myocilin is only associated with disease in the anterior segment of the eye, in the trabecular meshwork. The prevailing pathogenic mechanism involves a gain of toxic function whereby mutant myocilin aggregates intracellularly instead of being secreted, which causes cell stress and an early timeline for TM cell death, elevated intraocular pressure, and subsequent glaucoma-associated retinal degeneration. In this review, we focus on the work our lab has conducted over the past ∼15 years to enhance our molecular understanding of myocilin-associated glaucoma, which includes details of the molecular structure and the nature of the aggregates formed by mutant myocilin. We conclude by discussing open questions, such as predicting phenotype from genotype alone, the elusive native function of myocilin, and translational directions enabled by our work.

records.title: The pre-Descemet's layer (Dua's layer, also known as the Dua-Fine layer and the pre-posterior limiting lamina layer): Discovery, characterisation, clinical and surgical applications, and the controversy.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: The pre-Descemet's layer (Dua's layer, also known as the Dua-Fine layer and the pre-posterior limiting lamina layer): Discovery, characterisation, clinical and surgical applications, and the controversy.
content.abstract: The pre-Descemet's layer/Dua's layer, also termed the Dua-Fine layer and the pre-posterior limiting lamina layer, lies anterior to the Descemet's membrane in the cornea, is 10 μm (range 6-16) thick, made predominantly of type I and some type VI collagen with abundant elastin, more than any other layer of the cornea. It has high tensile strength (bursting pressure up to 700 mm of Hg), is impervious to air and almost acellular. At the periphery it demonstrates fenestrations and ramifies to become the core of the trabecular meshwork, with implications for intraocular pressure and glaucoma. It has been demonstrated in some species of animals. The layer has assumed considerable importance in anterior and posterior lamellar corneal transplant surgery by improving our understanding of the behaviour of corneal tissue during these procedures, improved techniques and made the surgery safer with better outcomes. It has led to the innovation of new surgical procedures namely, pre-Descemet's endothelial keratoplasty, suture management of acute hydrops, DALK-triple and Fogla's mini DALK. The discovery and knowledge of the layer has introduced paradigm shifts in our age old concepts of Descemet's membrane detachment, acute corneal hydrops in keratoconus and Descemetoceles, with impact on management approaches. It has been shown to contribute to the pathology and clinical signs observed in corneal infections and some corneal dystrophies. Early evidence suggests that it may have a role in the pathogenesis of keratoconus in relation to its elastin content. Its contribution to corneal biomechanics and glaucoma are subjects of current investigations.

records.title: Design and Conduct of Randomized Clinical Trials Evaluating Surgical Innovations in Ophthalmology: A Systematic Review.

content.title: Design and Conduct of Randomized Clinical Trials Evaluating Surgical Innovations in Ophthalmology: A Systematic Review.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Surgical innovations are necessary to improve patient care. After an initial exploratory phase, novel surgical technique should be compared with alternative options or standard care in randomized controlled trials (RCTs). However, surgical RCTs have unique methodological challenges. Our study sought to investigate key aspects of the design, conduct, and reporting of RCTs of novel surgeries.

Design

Systematic review.

Methods

The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD42021253297). RCTs evaluating novel surgeries for cataract, vitreoretinal, glaucoma, and corneal diseases were included. Medline, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, and Clinicaltrials.gov were searched. The search period was January 1, 2016, to June 16, 2021.

Results

A total of 52 ophthalmic surgery RCTs were identified in the fields of glaucoma (n = 12), vitreoretinal surgery (n = 5), cataract (n = 19), and cornea (n = 16). A description defining the surgeon's experience or level of expertise was reported in 30 RCTs (57%) and was presented in both control and intervention groups in 11 (21%). Specification of the number of cases performed in the particular surgical innovation being assessed prior to the trial was reported in 10 RCTs (19%) and an evaluation of quality of the surgical intervention in 7 (13%). Prospective trial registration was recorded in 12 RCTs (23%) and retrospective registration in 13 (25%); and there was no registration record in the remaining 28 (53%) studies.

Conclusions

Important aspects of the study design such as the surgical learning curve, surgeon's previous experience, quality assurance, and trial registration details were often missing in novel ophthalmic surgical procedures. The Idea, Development, Exploration, Assessment, Long-term follow-up (IDEAL) framework aims to improve the quality of study design.

records.title: The OCT angular sign of Henle fiber layer (HFL) hyperreflectivity (ASHH) and the pathoanatomy of the HFL in macular disease.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: The OCT angular sign of Henle fiber layer (HFL) hyperreflectivity (ASHH) and the pathoanatomy of the HFL in macular disease.
content.abstract: The Henle fiber layer (HFL) is comprised of bundles of unmyelinated photoreceptor axons intermingled with outer Müller cell processes. The photoreceptor axons extend from the cell bodies located in the outer nuclear layer and radially project toward the outer plexiform layer, the inner third of which includes the synaptic junctional complexes and the outer two-thirds of which includes the HFL. The oblique path of the HFL provides unique structural and reflectance properties and this radial anatomy is highlighted in many macular disorders including those with macular star exudation and HFL hemorrhage. Recent investigations using multimodal imaging techniques, especially cross sectional and en face optical coherence tomography (OCT), have provided new perspectives regarding HFL disruption in retinal diseases. The aim of this review is to highlight the pathoanatomy and multimodal imaging, especially OCT, associated with HFL disruption that is present in various macular diseases. After describing the current knowledge of the embryology, anatomy, and physiology of the HFL, we review the existing imaging modalities that allow in vivo visualization of the HFL in the healthy and diseased retina. Finally, we report the clinical and imaging findings of acute HFL alteration in various macular disorders, including degenerative, inflammatory, and vascular conditions. Also, we propose a novel and signature OCT biomarker indicative of acute photoreceptor disruption involving the HFL, termed the "angular sign of HFL hyperreflectivity" (ASHH) of macular disease, to unify the pathoanatomy common to these various macular disorders and to provide clarity regarding the underlying pathogenesis.

records.title: Studies of the retinal microcirculation using human donor eyes and high-resolution clinical imaging: Insights gained to guide future research in diabetic retinopathy.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Studies of the retinal microcirculation using human donor eyes and high-resolution clinical imaging: Insights gained to guide future research in diabetic retinopathy.
content.abstract: The microcirculation plays a key role in delivering oxygen to and removing metabolic wastes from energy-intensive retinal neurons. Microvascular changes are a hallmark feature of diabetic retinopathy (DR), a major cause of irreversible vision loss globally. Early investigators have performed landmark studies characterising the pathologic manifestations of DR. Previous works have collectively informed us of the clinical stages of DR and the retinal manifestations associated with devastating vision loss. Since these reports, major advancements in histologic techniques coupled with three-dimensional image processing has facilitated a deeper understanding of the structural characteristics in the healthy and diseased retinal circulation. Furthermore, breakthroughs in high-resolution retinal imaging have facilitated clinical translation of histologic knowledge to detect and monitor progression of microcirculatory disturbances with greater precision. Isolated perfusion techniques have been applied to human donor eyes to further our understanding of the cytoarchitectural characteristics of the normal human retinal circulation as well as provide novel insights into the pathophysiology of DR. Histology has been used to validate emerging in vivo retinal imaging techniques such as optical coherence tomography angiography. This report provides an overview of our research on the human retinal microcirculation in the context of the current ophthalmic literature. We commence by proposing a standardised histologic lexicon for characterising the human retinal microcirculation and subsequently discuss the pathophysiologic mechanisms underlying key manifestations of DR, with a focus on microaneurysms and retinal ischaemia. The advantages and limitations of current retinal imaging modalities as determined using histologic validation are also presented. We conclude with an overview of the implications of our research and provide a perspective on future directions in DR research.

records.title: Activation of retinal glial cells contributes to the degeneration of ganglion cells in experimental glaucoma.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Activation of retinal glial cells contributes to the degeneration of ganglion cells in experimental glaucoma.
content.abstract: Elevation of intraocular pressure (IOP) is a major risk factor for neurodegeneration in glaucoma. Glial cells, which play an important role in normal functioning of retinal neurons, are well involved into retinal ganglion cell (RGC) degeneration in experimental glaucoma animal models generated by elevated IOP. In response to elevated IOP, mGluR I is first activated and Kir4.1 channels are subsequently inhibited, which leads to the activation of Müller cells. Müller cell activation is followed by a complex process, including proliferation, release of inflammatory and growth factors (gliosis). Gliosis is further regulated by several factors. Activated Müller cells contribute to RGC degeneration through generating glutamate receptor-mediated excitotoxicity, releasing cytotoxic factors and inducing microglia activation. Elevated IOP activates microglia, and following morphological and functional changes, these cells, as resident immune cells in the retina, show adaptive immune responses, including an enhanced release of pro-inflammatory factors (tumor neurosis factor-α, interleukins, etc.). These ATP and Toll-like receptor-mediated responses are further regulated by heat shock proteins, CD200R, chemokine receptors, and metabotropic purinergic receptors, may aggravate RGC loss. In the optic nerve head, astrogliosis is initiated and regulated by a complex reaction process, including purines, transmitters, chemokines, growth factors and cytokines, which contributes to RGC axon injury through releasing pro-inflammatory factors and changing extracellular matrix in glaucoma. The effects of activated glial cells on RGCs are further modified by the interplay among different types of glial cells. This review is concluded by presenting an in-depth discussion of possible research directions in this field in the future.

records.title: Advances in understanding the molecular structure of retinoschisin while questions remain of biological function.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Advances in understanding the molecular structure of retinoschisin while questions remain of biological function.
content.abstract: Retinoschisin (RS1) is a secreted protein that is essential for maintaining integrity of the retina. Numerous mutations in RS1 cause X-linked retinoschisis (XLRS), a progressive degeneration of the retina that leads to vision loss in young males. A key manifestation of XLRS is the formation of cavities (cysts) in the retina and separation of the layers (schisis), disrupting synaptic transmission. There are currently no approved treatments for patients with XLRS. Strategies using adeno-associated viral (AAV) vectors to deliver functional copies of RS1 as a form of gene augmentation therapy, are under clinical evaluation. To improve therapeutic strategies for treating XLRS, it is critical to better understand the secretion of RS1 and its molecular function. Immunofluorescence and immunoelectron microscopy show that RS1 is located on the surfaces of the photoreceptor inner segments and bipolar cells. Sequence homology indicates a discoidin domain fold, similar to many other proteins with demonstrated adhesion functions. Recent structural studies revealed the tertiary structure of RS1 as two back-to-back octameric rings, each cross-linked by disulfides. The observation of higher order structures in vitro suggests the formation of an adhesive matrix spanning the distance between cells (∼100 nm). Several studies indicated that RS1 readily binds to other proteins such as the sodium-potassium ATPase (NaK-ATPase) and extracellular matrix proteins. Alternatively, RS1 may influence fluid regulation via interaction with membrane proteins such as the NaK-ATPase, largely inferred from the use of carbonic anhydrase inhibitors to shrink the typical intra-retinal cysts in XLRS. We discuss these models in light of RS1 structure and address the difficulty in understanding the function of RS1.

records.title: Genome-wide Survival Analysis for Macular Neovascularization Development in Central Serous Chorioretinopathy Revealed Shared Genetic Susceptibility with Polypoidal Choroidal Vasculopathy.

content.title: Genome-wide Survival Analysis for Macular Neovascularization Development in Central Serous Chorioretinopathy Revealed Shared Genetic Susceptibility with Polypoidal Choroidal Vasculopathy.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To identify susceptibility genes for macular neovascularization (MNV) development in central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC).

Design

Genome-wide survival analysis using a longitudinal cohort study.

Participants

We included 402 and 137 patients with CSC but without MNV at their first visit from the Kyoto CSC Cohort and Kobe CSC dataset, respectively. All patients underwent detailed ophthalmic examinations, including multimodal imaging, such as fundus autofluorescence, spectral-domain OCT, and fluorescein angiography/indocyanine green angiography or OCT angiography.

Methods

We conducted a genome-wide survival analysis using the Kyoto CSC Cohort. We applied the Cox proportional hazard model to adjust for age, sex, and the first principal component. Single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) with P values < 1.0 × 10-5 were carried forward to the replication in the Kobe CSC dataset. Moreover, we evaluated the contribution of previously reported age-related macular degeneration (AMD) susceptibility loci. We used FUMA and ToppFun for the functional enrichment analysis.

Main outcome measures

The association between SNPs and MNV development in patients with CSC.

Results

Rs370974631 near ARMS2 displayed a genome-wide significant association in the meta-analysis of discovery and replication result (hazard ratio [HR]meta, 3.63; Pmeta = 5.76 × 10-9). Among previously reported AMD susceptibility loci, we additionally identified CFH rs800292 (HR, 0.39, P = 2.55 × 10-4), COL4A3 rs4276018 (HR, 0.26, P = 1.56 × 10-3), and B3GALTL rs9564692 (HR, 0.56, P = 8.30 × 10-3) as susceptibility loci for MNV development in CSC. The functional enrichment analysis revealed significant enrichment of 8 pathways (GO:0051561, GO:0036444, GO:0008282, GO:1990246, GO:0015272, GO:0030955, GO:0031420, and GO:0005242) related to ion transport.

Conclusions

ARMS2, CFH, COL4A3, and B3GALTL were identified as susceptibility genes for MNV development in CSC. These 4 genes are known as susceptibility genes for AMD, whereas COL4A3 and B3GALTL were previously reported to be polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy (PCV)-specific susceptibility genes. Our findings revealed the shared genetic susceptibility between PCV and MNV secondary to CSC.

records.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.

content.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Current AI models for optical coherence tomography (OCT) primarily focus on diagnosis as a standalone task. We developed and validated an end-to-end agentic AI workflow that integrates automated macular hole (MH) diagnosis from OCT images with structured patient-friendly report generation.

Methods

The proposed sequential workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent consisted of an image diagnosis stage and a language generation step. The OCT version of RETFound, a self-supervised retinal foundation model, was fine-tuned for binary classification of macular OCT scans as MH or normal macula. Training, validation, and internal testing were performed using multiple public OCT datasets with patient-level stratified splitting, followed by external validation on two independent datasets. The performance of the fine-tuned foundation model was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC AUC). For each new OCT image, the AI agent used the trained RETFound model to classify the image, received the diagnostic output, incorporated it into a structured prompt, and called the large language model (GPT-4) to generate the clinical report.

Results

On the internal test set (n = 180), the model achieved an accuracy of 100% (95% confidence interval (CI), 97.9-100%) with an AUC of 1.00. On external validation (n = 1014), accuracy was 98.8% (95% CI 97.9-99.3%), sensitivity was 97.9% (95% CI 96.3-98.8%), specificity was 100% (95% CI 99.2-100.0%), and AUC was 0.999 (95% CI 0.998-1.000). Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) analysis showed that predictions were driven by relevant retinal regions, particularly the macular hole and adjacent layers. The end-to-end agentic AI workflow generated concise and standardized patient-friendly reports for all samples, without the language model influencing diagnostic decisions.

Conclusions

This study demonstrates the feasibility of an end-to-end AI workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent for robust OCT-based MH diagnosis with a large language model for structured report generation. By separating image-based diagnosis from language generation, this approach offers a practical and scalable solution for virtual vitreoretinal clinics.

records.title: Assessment of peripapillary choroidal microvascular structure in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus using a deep learning-based approach.
records.publisher: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie

content.title: Assessment of peripapillary choroidal microvascular structure in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus using a deep learning-based approach.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate peripapillary choroidal microvascular structure in patients with idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) using a novel deep learning-based approach, and to evaluate longitudinal changes following shunt surgery.

Methods

In this prospective study, 22 patients with iNPH and 22 age-matched healthy controls underwent peripapillary optical coherence tomography (OCT). A deep learning-based ResUNet model enabled choroidal segmentation and quantification of total choroidal area (TCA), stromal choroidal area (SCA), luminal choroidal area (LCA), and the choroidal vascularity index (CVI). Measurements were compared between groups and reassessed in iNPH patients after ventriculoperitoneal shunt surgery.

Results

Forty-four eyes of 22 iNPH patients and 44 eyes of 22 controls were analyzed. iNPH eyes exhibited significantly greater mean SCA compared to controls (adjusted p < 0.05). On the other hand, CVI remained comparable between groups. Following a mean follow-up of approximately 12 months after shunt surgery, mean SCA showed significant reduction (adjusted p < 0.05), whereas CVI remained unchanged.

Conclusions

iNPH was associated with peripapillary choroidal changes, predominantly involving the stromal compartment. Deep learning-based OCT analysis may provide a noninvasive approach for quantifying peripapillary choroidal microstructure, although the clinical relevance of these findings remains to be established.

records.title: Early Diagnosis and Prognosis of Corneal and Ocular Surface Pathologies Using Artificial Intelligence: A State-of-the-art Review.

content.title: Early Diagnosis and Prognosis of Corneal and Ocular Surface Pathologies Using Artificial Intelligence: A State-of-the-art Review.
content.abstract:
Purpose

This study aims to elucidate the expanding role of artificial intelligence (AI) in the early diagnosis of corneal and ocular surface diseases. AI has the potential to enhance diagnostic precision, streamline clinical workflows, and facilitate disease detection before clinical manifestations become evident.

Methods

A narrative literature review was conducted to assess the impact of AI and machine learning in corneal disease preclinical diagnosis. A comprehensive search in PubMed was performed using key terms such as "artificial intelligence," "machine learning," "deep learning," "corneal diseases," and "early diagnosis." Eligible studies were those published in English over the last decade that focused on AI-driven diagnostic approaches and prognostic modeling. Case reports, nonoriginal studies, and those with minimal AI integration were excluded. Data extraction emphasized AI methodologies, imaging techniques, diagnostic performance metrics, and clinical relevance.

Results

AI-powered machine learning models analyze vast imaging datasets, detecting subclinical abnormalities imperceptible to conventional diagnostic methods. This capability is particularly significant in early keratoconus detection, dystrophies, infectious keratitis, conjunctival neoplasia, and other corneal pathologies such as dry eye or Steven-Johnson disease, where subtle morphological changes precede clinically apparent disease.

Conclusions

The integration of AI into corneal disease diagnostics and management could mark in the future a transformative shift in Ophthalmology, offering precision, efficiency, and scalability. By facilitating early disease detection and individualized patient assessments, AI minimizes diagnostic inconsistencies and accelerates clinical decision making. Continuous algorithm refinement and real-world validation are crucial to maximizing AI's clinical utility. To fully harness AI's potential, multidisciplinary collaboration among ophthalmologists, data scientists, and regulatory bodies is imperative to address standardization, ethical concerns, and implementation barriers. As AI-driven technologies continue to evolve, they will redefine the standard of care in corneal disease diagnosis, therapeutic precision, and patient outcomes.

records.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.

content.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.
content.abstract:
Background

Increasing use of large language models in nursing education has raised questions about the association between reliance on these tools and academic distress. This study examined direct and specific indirect associations between large language model dependence (LMD) and academic anxiety (AA) through artificial intelligence addiction (AIA) and academic burnout (AB).

Methods

A cross-sectional survey was conducted from March to April 2026 among 473 nursing students in Guangdong Province, China, including students undertaking clinical placements. The four constructs were assessed using items selected from published self-report instruments. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was performed with age and sex included as covariates. Direct and specific indirect associations were evaluated using bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples.

Results

Cronbach's α ranged from 0.914 to 0.944, composite reliability from 0.935 to 0.954, and average variance extracted from 0.560 to 0.721. Heterotrait-monotrait ratios ranged from 0.485 to 0.733, supporting discriminant validity. Model fit evidence was mixed: SRMR was 0.068, whereas NFI was 0.812, below the 0.90 reference value. The model explained 49.2% of the variance in academic anxiety. Large language model dependence showed a small positive direct association with academic anxiety (β = 0.138, 95% CI [0.006, 0.278], p = 0.048). Significant specific indirect associations were identified through academic burnout (β = 0.205, 95% CI [0.123, 0.303]) and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout (β = 0.098, 95% CI [0.049, 0.147]); both p < 0.001.

Conclusion

Large language model dependence was positively associated with academic anxiety among nursing students, with specific indirect associations through academic burnout and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout. These findings highlight the relevance of problematic AI use and study-related exhaustion to academic distress. However, the cross-sectional design does not establish temporal ordering or causal mediation.

records.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.

content.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.
content.abstract:
Aims

Whether a retinal artificial intelligence (AI) risk score reclassifies SCORE2 cardiovascular risk stratification in statin-naive adults across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary is uncertain. We evaluated the retinal AI risk score for 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) prediction.

Methods

In 40,672 statin-naive UK Biobank participants (aged 40-69, without diabetes), cardiovascular risk categories and treatment recommendation status (Class I or IIa vs neither) were defined using the 2025 ESC/EAS focused-update framework. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) adjusted for SCORE2 or for established risk factors. The incremental predictive value of adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation.

Results

Over a 10.0-year median follow-up (914 ASCVD events), the very high retinal AI risk group independently predicted ASCVD (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.32 vs low risk; p<0.001). Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 reclassified risk across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary (statin-eligibility NRI [net reclassification improvement] 0.012, p<0.001); reclassification was statistically significant but modest (continuous NRI 0.445, p<0.001), without C-index or net-benefit gain. In the statin-indicated subgroup, retinal AI risk groups further stratified risk (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.16; p<0.001). Statin-not-indicated participants in the high or very high retinal AI risk groups had numerically similar observed 10-year risk to all statin-indicated, untreated participants (p=0.758). There was no evidence of effect modification by clinically detectable retinal disorder (interaction p=0.93). Incremental value was greater in women than men (sex interaction p<0.001).

Conclusion

Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 produced modest bidirectional risk reclassification across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary; these findings warrant prospective validation.Abstract word count: 250 words.

records.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.

content.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.
content.abstract:
Background

The eye and the kidney share microvascular features, and retinal changes have been postulated to reflect systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. Recently, retinal age, estimated by deep learning (DL) from a single fundus photograph, has been shown to predict cardiovascular events. The present study aimed to determine whether retinal aging speed, defined as the individual-specific annual rate of change in DL-estimated retinal age, is associated with rapid estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed the longitudinal data obtained from 7807 Japanese individuals who underwent repeated health check-ups with serial measurements of eGFR and fundus photographs (median 9.0 visits over median 8.0 years). We evaluated the relationship between retinal aging speed during the baseline period (from baseline to year 4) and rapid eGFR decline (≤ -3 ml/min/1.73 m²/year) during the follow-up period (after year 4).

Results

The incidence of rapid eGFR decline was significantly higher in the highest quartile of retinal aging speed than in the lowest quartile as the reference group in the fully adjusted model adjusting age, sex, body mass index, blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, eGFR, and proteinuria [odds ratio (OR) 1.34; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.06-1.68; P = .015]. In the multivariable logistic regression models, retinal aging speed was associated with rapid eGFR decline after adjusting multiple key confounders (OR 1.14; 95% CI 1.02-1.29; P = .027).

Conclusions

Taken together, DL-derived retinal aging speed is independently associated with rapid eGFR decline in the Japanese general population.

records.title: Mapping Research on AI-Based Computer-Aided Diagnosis and Clinical Decision Support Systems: a Bibliometric Study Integrating Google Trends and Content Analysis.

content.title: Mapping Research on AI-Based Computer-Aided Diagnosis and Clinical Decision Support Systems: a Bibliometric Study Integrating Google Trends and Content Analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Research on artificial intelligence-based computer-aided diagnosis and clinical decision support systems (AI-CDSS) is expanding, but integrated evidence on publication patterns, keyword trajectories, online search activity, and methodological characteristics remains limited.

Objective

To characterize AI-CDSS research by integrating bibliometric analysis, Google Trends comparison, and structured content analysis of citation-ranked publications.

Methods

Scholarly interest was assessed using bibliometric analysis of Web of Science records from 2016 through August 2026, including author-keyword co-occurrence, bibliographic coupling, and reference co-citation, whereas Google Trends was used to characterize online search activity. A structured content analysis of citation-ranked publications was conducted to examine applications, methodological characteristics, and reported limitations.

Results

We analyzed 19,809 included publications from 2016 through August 2026. Output rose approximately 21-fold, from 193 records in 2016 to 4,082 in 2025. Output was geographically concentrated within the included corpus, with a Gini coefficient of 0.869. Among records with identifiable corresponding-author country or territory, China, the United States, and India accounted for 61.33%. Scientific Reports was the most frequent source (n = 916). Frequent artificial intelligence- and diagnosis-related keywords included machine learning (n = 5,666), deep learning (n = 4,022), and computer-aided diagnosis (n = 1,512). Bibliographic coupling identified 15 publication communities, and reference co-citation identified seven reference communities. In the monthly level-series comparison, 9 of 10 keyword concepts exhibited significant associations with Google Trends relative search interest, but none of the 10 first-difference associations remained significant after Bonferroni adjustment. Content analysis of 215 citation-ranked publications, including 191 empirical publications, showed frequent use of convolutional neural networks in diagnostic and radiology applications. Common limitations included limited external validation, infrequent calibration reporting, and sparse workflow-level or impact evaluation.

Conclusion

AI-CDSS research has rapidly expanded around machine learning, deep learning, and diagnostic applications, but the analyzed citation-ranked publications provide more evidence of methodological development than of clinical deployment. Integrating bibliometric, search-activity, and content-based perspectives shows limited short-term correspondence between online search activity and scholarly keyword use and highlights the need to move beyond model development toward independent external validation, prospective workflow and patient-outcome evaluation, calibration, fairness, and postdeployment monitoring.

records.title: Digital Health and Artificial Intelligence for Public Health Systems in Africa: A Narrative Review.

content.title: Digital Health and Artificial Intelligence for Public Health Systems in Africa: A Narrative Review.
content.abstract:
Background and aims

Digital health and artificial intelligence (AI) are promoted as ways to strengthen African public health systems, but the evidence is fragmented across technologies, settings, and levels of rigor. This review synthesized evidence on mobile health (mHealth), telemedicine, and AI in Africa to examine what works, where and under which conditions, and the ethical, regulatory, and equity implications.

Methods

Narrative review guided by the SANRA criteria. PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar were searched for literature published from January 2010 to May 2025, supplemented by gray literature from WHO, Africa CDC, and the African Union; quantitative claims were re-verified against original sources in October 2026. Evidence was organized using a framework linking three technology tiers to health system building blocks and appraised by study design and, for AI, by validation stage.

Results

The most consistent evidence concerned text messaging: in African randomized trials, one-way SMS improved appointment attendance (odds ratio 2.03) and two-way SMS improved medicine adherence (risk ratio 1.14). Programs that reached national scale were government-led and aligned with existing information systems, and in Rwanda were effective only alongside wider health system support. Telemedicine evidence was largely descriptive; AI evidence consisted mainly of development, and accuracy studies; computer-aided tuberculosis detection had pooled sensitivity of 0.87 and specificity of 0.74 in studies at high risk of bias, and patient-outcome evidence was scarce. Although 38 of 47 WHO African Region Member States reported national digital health strategies, only 9 of 34 publicly available strategies were rated strong. Connectivity, electricity, training, data protection, and donor dependence were barriers, distributed unequally by education, location, and gender.

Conclusion

Simple, interoperable, government-led tools have the strongest evidence of benefit at scale in Africa. AI requires prospective, locally validated evaluation of patient outcomes, and investment should prioritize governance, interoperability, inclusion, and sustainable domestic financing.

records.title: Automated assessment of healthcare de-escalation communication skills in a conversational AI virtual reality simulation.

content.title: Automated assessment of healthcare de-escalation communication skills in a conversational AI virtual reality simulation.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Digital health training environments increasingly require scalable methods for assessing communication skills in realistic, interactive scenarios. This paper presents a comparative study of automated assessment approaches within a conversational AI virtual reality simulation designed for verbal de-escalation training.

Methods

A total of 20 nursing students completed the simulation, where their spoken responses were captured and converted to text through a speech-to-text system, and were evaluated across 11 de-escalation competencies. The evaluation compared three fine-tuned deep learning models (BERT, RoBERTa, and XLNet) with a modified RATAS, a rubric-driven framework that leverages large language models. Two experiments were conducted: one using controlled 100-item validation datasets for each section, and another using the real-world responses collected during the user study.

Results

On the validation datasets, the deep learning models achieved the highest performance, with RoBERTa obtaining an average accuracy of 0.9927, followed by BERT at 0.9900 and XLNet at 0.9790, while RATAS achieved 0.8554. On the student-response dataset, performance decreased for all approaches, with RoBERTa obtaining 0.8590 accuracy, RATAS 0.8181, BERT 0.8000, and XLNet 0.7681.

Discussion

These results suggest that transformer-based models perform best under controlled conditions, whereas RATAS demonstrated stability in grading across different dataset types. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of integrating deep learning and rubric-driven LLM-based automated assessment approaches for communication and de-escalation training in nursing education.

records.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.

content.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Echocardiography has evolved substantially since its introduction in 1954. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers transformative potential for image acquisition, quantification, interpretation, and reporting. Despite growing research interest, a comprehensive evaluation of the historical trends and evolution of AI in echocardiography is lacking. The study aimed to conduct a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of the global research landscape in this field.

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted using the Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection databases for publications on AI in echocardiography from inception through November 10, 2025; no language filter was applied. Data analysis was performed using Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Access, and IBM SPSS Statistics. In addition, bibliometric mapping and data visualization were conducted.

Results

Overall, 2682 publications received 35,083 citations (mean, 13.08 citations per publication), spanning 1984-2025. Original articles, conference papers, and review articles accounted for 87.4% and 98.5% of total publications and citations, respectively. Publication output remained limited until approximately 2015, rose gradually thereafter, and accelerated markedly after 2018, with similar output in 2024 and 2025. The United States led in both publication volume and total citations, followed by China and the United Kingdom. The United States also had the highest collaboration link strength, and seven of the top 10 institutions were in North America (six in the United States and one in Canada). Mayo Clinic ranked first, with 142 publications and 3604 citations, and had the earliest first indexed publication among the top institutions (1992). The journal JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging ranked first in both total citations (1,911) and citations per publication (36.75). "Echocardiography," "deep learning," "artificial intelligence," and "machine learning" were the most frequently used terms. The thematic evolution showed continuity of algorithmic-centric themes (1984-2019) with emerging clinically oriented themes (2020-2025).

Conclusions

This comprehensive bibliometric analysis highlights the rapid expansion of AI research in echocardiography, characterized by an accelerating publication output and emerging clinically oriented research topics. These findings reflect growing research interest in integrating AI into echocardiographic practice and highlight the need for future research prioritizing multicenter validation, clinical translation, and equitable real-world implementation.

records.title: Beyond scales: Artificial intelligence, language, and behavior in suicide risk modeling-a narrative review.
records.publisher: European neuropsychopharmacology : the journal of the European College of Neuropsychopharmacology

content.title: Beyond scales: Artificial intelligence, language, and behavior in suicide risk modeling-a narrative review.
content.abstract: Suicide is a leading, preventable cause of premature mortality, yet identifying individuals at imminent risk remains difficult. There are no validated biomarkers for routine stratification, and common approaches (clinical interviews, rating scales, self-report) are limited by subjectivity, reporting bias, and weak positive predictive value for rare outcomes. Rapid advances in artificial intelligence (AI)-including machine learning, deep learning, and large language models-offer opportunities to integrate heterogeneous signals relevant to risk and treatment response. This narrative review summarizes recent AI-enabled prediction and characterization of suicidal thoughts and behaviors across major data modalities: structured electronic health records and claims; natural language processing of clinical notes and digital text; speech and facial/behavioral signals; neuroimaging and other neurobiological measures; and passive sensing from smartphones and wearables. We review common modeling and evaluation practices, emphasizing clinically relevant performance assessment (discrimination and calibration) and the importance of temporal and external validation. We also highlight barriers to translation, including class imbalance and label noise, dataset shift across sites and time, limited prospective evaluation, and the need for interpretable outputs that can support medication decisions and care pathways (e.g., triage, monitoring, and stepped interventions). Ethical and implementation challenges-privacy and consent, algorithmic bias and equity, governance, and the clinical consequences of false-positive and false-negative predictions-are discussed with an emphasis on safe deployment. We conclude with priorities for the field, including multimodal longitudinal cohorts, harmonized reporting standards, and pragmatic trials to determine whether AI decision support measurably improves suicide-prevention outcomes.

records.title: Application of an Artificial Intelligence Simulated Patient Model in Teaching Neurosurgical Decision-Making.

content.title: Application of an Artificial Intelligence Simulated Patient Model in Teaching Neurosurgical Decision-Making.
content.abstract:
Aim

Training in neurosurgical decision-making remains a challenging component of standardized residency training. Traditional teaching models are limited in their ability to simulate the uncertainty and complexity encountered in real-world clinical scenarios. As a novel educational tool, the potential value of artificial intelligence (AI)-simulated patient models in surgical decision-making training requires further evaluation. This study aimed to explore the application of an AI-simulated patient model in neurosurgical decision-making education and to assess its effectiveness in improving residents' clinical decision-making abilities.

Methods

A retrospective study was conducted involving 157 residents who underwent standardized residency training in the Department of Neurosurgery from January 2023 to April 2026. Based on the implementation of the AI-simulated teaching model beginning in January 2025, participants were divided into two groups according to the teaching model used: an experimental group (n = 72, receiving AI-simulated patient teaching from January 2025 to April 2026) and a control group (n = 85, receiving traditional case discussion teaching from January 2023 to December 2024). The experimental group used a large language model-based virtual patient system powered by DeepSeek to perform dialogue-driven history taking, image interpretation, surgical planning, and risk prediction with real-time feedback, while the control group received conventional methods. After teaching, an objective structured clinical examination (OSCE) was used to assess surgical decision-making across five dimensions, including localization diagnosis, surgical approach, risk identification, emergency management, and surgical timing, and a questionnaire was used to measure teaching satisfaction.

Results

The total score for surgical decision-making ability was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.001). Dimensional analysis showed that localization diagnosis, surgical method selection, risk identification, emergency response, and surgical timing judgment were higher in the experimental group than in the control group (all p < 0.05). The excellent rate for each assessment dimension (>85 points) was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.05). The satisfaction score was also higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.001).

Conclusions

The AI-simulated patient model based on a general-purpose large language model was associated with better surgical decision-making performance among neurosurgery residents. It has significant advantages in localization diagnosis, surgical approach selection, risk identification, emergency response, and judgment of surgical timing, and is well accepted by residents.

records.title: Impact of Image Bit Depth Reduction on Deep Learning Performance in Chest Radiograph Analysis: A Multi-institutional Study.

content.title: Impact of Image Bit Depth Reduction on Deep Learning Performance in Chest Radiograph Analysis: A Multi-institutional Study.
content.abstract:
Rationale and objectives

Medical imaging typically generates 12-bit to 16-bit formats, yet conversion to 8-bit is often required. While deep learning has been widely explored in medical imaging, the influence of image bit depth on model performance is not fully understood. This study evaluates the impact of conversion from 16-bit to 8-bit for sex, age, and obesity classification using deep learning.

Materials and methods

In this retrospective, multi-institutional study, we analyzed 100,002 chest radiographs from 48,047 participants across three institutions. Images were uniformly quantized from the fixed 0-65535 range to 256 levels (0-255) with no additional processing. Three convolutional neural network architectures (ResNet52, EfficientNetB2, and ConvNeXtSmall) were trained on both 16-bit and 8-bit versions of the images. Model performance was evaluated using internal test datasets, randomly split multiple times, and an external test dataset. Statistical analysis included paired comparisons of area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) values, with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons.

Results

Across all architectures and classification tasks, differences between 16-bit and 8-bit model performance were minimal (mean differences ranging from -0.218%-0.184%). Statistical analyses revealed no significant differences in AUC-ROC values between bit depths for any model-task combination (all p values > 0.05 after Bonferroni correction). Effect sizes were small to moderate (Cohen's d ranging from -0.415-0.391).

Conclusion

No statistically significant differences were detected between models trained on 16-bit and 8-bit images in the three evaluated tasks. These findings suggest that conversion to 8-bit images may reduce data storage requirements and improve data processing efficiency. Further research is needed to assess their usefulness in clinical tasks.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.
content.abstract:
Background

Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in women globally, accounting for approximately 2.30 million new cases and 666,103 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence technologies including machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and natural language processing have been widely applied across the breast cancer care continuum. However, no systematic review restricted to primary studies with patient-level or image-level data has synthesized evidence spanning all clinical domains simultaneously.

Objectives

To evaluate the performance, methodological quality, and clinical relevance of artificial intelligence primary studies across screening and diagnostic imaging, digital pathology, radiomics, perioperative management, prognostic prediction, and natural language processing in breast cancer.

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2015 to May 2026. Eligibility was restricted to original primary research reporting patient-level or image-level data; secondary syntheses were explicitly excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

Results

Of 5,275 identified records, 17 primary studies met eligibility criteria. In screening mammography (seven studies; n = 7,540 to 144,231 examinations), deep learning achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.876 to 0.939; a randomised trial in 80,033 women demonstrated non-inferiority to double reading with a 44.3% reduction in radiologist workload. In digital pathology (five studies; 270 to 44,732 whole-slide images), deep learning achieved AUC 0.985 to 0.994, exceeding unassisted pathologist performance in lymph node metastasis detection. Magnetic resonance imaging radiomics predicted pathological complete response in HER2-positive breast cancer with AUC 0.80. No breast cancer-specific perioperative primary study met the eligibility criteria. Deep survival networks achieved concordance index 0.626 versus 0.612 for Cox regression in breast cancer cohorts. Natural language processing identified metastatic recurrence in breast cancer clinical records with sensitivity 83% and specificity 73%. Risk of bias was low to moderate for imaging and pathology studies and high for small sample radiomics studies. Density-stratified performance was reported by only two imaging studies, and receptor status prediction from haematoxylin and eosin staining had not been validated as a safe alternative to immunohistochemistry.

Conclusions

Artificial intelligence demonstrated clinically meaningful performance across the five domains with eligible primary studies. Breast cancer-specific perioperative and intensive care primary studies were absent, representing the largest evidence gap. External validation, demographic diversity, and prospective clinical integration evidence remained the most consistently identified limitations. Prediction of molecular receptor status without immunohistochemistry requires rigorous prospective safety validation before it can complement standard testing.

records.title: Digital twin oncology and multi-omics-driven artificial intelligence models for personalized drug response prediction: A systematic survey of emerging computational paradigms and clinical implementation challenges.

content.title: Digital twin oncology and multi-omics-driven artificial intelligence models for personalized drug response prediction: A systematic survey of emerging computational paradigms and clinical implementation challenges.
content.abstract: The increasing complexity of tumor heterogeneity and variable therapeutic response has intensified the need for accurate personalized drug response prediction in oncology. Traditional trial-and-error chemotherapy strategies often result in suboptimal outcomes, toxicity, and delayed therapeutic adjustments. Rapid advances in multi-omics technologies, artificial intelligence (AI) and digital twin modeling have significantly reshaped computational oncology research. This survey systematically reviews peer-reviewed research and review articles published from 2021 onward that investigate emerging computational paradigms integrating digital twins and multi-omics AI for drug response prediction. The foundational concepts in digital twin oncology, multi-omics profiling and AI-driven precision medicine are outlined initially. The existing approaches are categorized into four major paradigms such as omics-driven machine learning models, deep learning based multimodal architectures, mechanistic digital twin simulation frameworks and hybrid digital twin AI systems enabling adaptive therapy optimization. The multi-omics data integration strategies, including early, intermediate, late, network-based and graph/pathway-based fusion techniques. The survey synthesizes recent developments in drug sensitivity prediction, immunotherapy response modeling, tumor evolution forecasting and virtual clinical trials, while critically analyzing challenges related to data heterogeneity, interpretability, generalization, privacy, regulatory compliance and ethical considerations. Finally, future directions are highlighted such as real-time adaptive digital twins, federated learning, explainable AI and regulatory ready clinical deployment frameworks. Overall, this review provides a structured taxonomy, comparative analysis and research roadmap for advancing integrated digital twin and multi omics AI systems toward clinically actionable precision oncology.

records.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.

content.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), especially the recent proliferation of generative Large Language Models (LLMs), is transforming traditional anatomy education by introducing new teaching tools. However, the adoption of these cutting-edge technologies raises questions about global educational equity. It remains unclear whether AI will serve as a digital equalizer or further exacerbate marginalization. This rapid bibliometric synthesis aims to provide a comprehensive, data-driven overview of the "Application of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education" (AAAE). We seek to map the intellectual landscape, detect structural and technological shifts, evaluate the geopolitical disparities, and provide corresponding references. A total of 85 consolidated records were retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. These data constituted the whole panorama of AAAE. Bibliometrix and CiteSpace were utilized for static and dynamic mapping. A multidisciplinary expert panel validated the thematic clusters using Gwet's AC1 and the Normalized Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI). Publications surged following ChatGPT's release, indicating a shift from specialized computer vision to the application of general-purpose LLMs. While high-income countries maintain leadership, AI could exert a "democratizing effect" on upper-middle-income countries, doubling their odds of publication compared to traditional anatomy. Six research frontiers and three research trajectories were captured, and corresponding implications for future researchers in the global south and north were presented. AAAE could be conducted using a stratified strategy: different expansions of AI technologies for pedagogy; leveraging commercial APIs to bypass infrastructure bottlenecks; and validating open-source models. Global equity critically demands cross-border collaboration and inclusive datasets.

records.title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.

content.title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to conventional oral photographs for recognition, classification, localization, segmentation, and risk assessment of oral mucosal lesions. This systematic review evaluated how clinically relevant visual information-including color, texture, morphology, borders, and spatial patterns-is represented by AI systems and assessed performance, validation, explainability, human comparison, and clinical translation. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for studies directly analyzing conventional white-light clinical photographs. Risk of bias was assessed with PROBAST + AI, and certainty with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation-based approaches. Fifty-three studies were included, 30 published in 2025-2026. Forty-six used implicit deep-learning visual representations, three multimodal vision-language models, two explicit color analyses, and two explicit texture analyses. Thirty-one studies primarily addressed image-level diagnostic classification/recognition, 15 spatial detection/localization or lesion delineation, six screening/triage/referral or biopsy-oriented decision support, and one longitudinal malignant-transformation prediction. Six used independent external cohorts and five compared AI with human readers. Methodological concerns were frequent, no sufficiently coherent group supported meta-analysis, and certainty remained limited across evidence bodies. Current evidence therefore supports technical feasibility rather than established clinical effectiveness, with translation requiring stronger patient-level independence, external validation, prospective multicenter evaluation, and evidence of clinical benefit.

records.title: A review of deep learning applications on histopathologic and genomic data in focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.

content.title: A review of deep learning applications on histopathologic and genomic data in focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.
content.abstract: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis explains the histological pattern of injury seen through light microscopy in kidney biopsy specimens and is the end result of different injuries to podocytes. The clinical classification of patients by FSGS lesion is challenging because of a broad spectrum of etiologies, limited understanding of pathophysiology, and poor correlation among histopathology, treatment response, and clinical outcomes. Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis is a problematic process to detect lesions, with low and late analysis of the absence of initial symptoms, and a challenging position of specific markers. However, Histopathological and genomic Data in Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) are significantly used in multiple research applications, but they face several limitations that restrict the efficiency of experimental analysis. This review systematically analyzed recent enhancements in biopsy-based analysis and deep learning models for FSGS, with specific emphasis on different mechanisms. Moreover, this review analyzed different strategies, namely kidney transplantation, pathogenesis to therapeutic approaches, transformer-based architectures, glomerular segmentation methodologies, multitasking strategy classification, and gene expression analysis for FSGS. This review analysis includes 121 research papers, which are selected and analyzed for glomerular segmentation, gene expression, clinical outcomes, lesion classification, and disease recurrence prediction. Based on the recent research frameworks, it explicitly states the performance analysis, benefits, as well as challenges of FSGS. The article presents details of a new dataset and future directions for improving the majority of nephropathology diagnoses previously available through the use of integrated approaches that utilize both histopathology and genomics, enhancing future research direction in FSGS.

records.title: Factors associated with postoperative delirium in patients undergoing oral and maxillofacial surgery: a meta-analysis of observational study.

content.title: Factors associated with postoperative delirium in patients undergoing oral and maxillofacial surgery: a meta-analysis of observational study.
content.abstract:
Background

Postoperative delirium (POD) is a common and serious complication, particularly prevalent among patients undergoing oral and maxillofacial surgery (OMFS). Although studies have explored risk factors for POD, a systematic assessment for OMFS patients remains lacking. This study aimed to identify and synthesize factors associated with POD in patients undergoing OMFS. However, the currently available evidence appears to be derived mainly from major oncologic and reconstructive OMFS populations.

Methods

The literature search was conducted from the establishment of the database to December 10, 2025, covering PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science. All studies involving POD in patients undergoing OMFS were included in the analysis. The quality of included studies was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). Data analysis was performed using Stata 15 software, employing a random-effects model for meta-analysis of potential risk factors.

Results

A total of seven studies involving 2,398 patients were included. The meta-analysis showed that age >65 years [OR = 1.63, 95% CI (1.15, 2.31)], male sex [OR = 1.90, 95% CI (1.17, 3.09)], alcohol consumption [OR = 3.43, 95% CI (2.09, 5.66)], smoking [OR = 2.34, 95% CI (1.19, 4.59)], and insomnia [OR = 2.27, 95% CI (1.24, 4.19)] were associated with POD in patients undergoing OMFS.

Conclusion

This study suggests that age >65 years, male sex, alcohol consumption, smoking, and insomnia may be associated with POD in patients undergoing OMFS. However, the available evidence is derived predominantly from major oral cancer and reconstructive surgery populations, and all included studies were observational. Therefore, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal risk factors, and their applicability to the broader spectrum of OMFS procedures remains uncertain.

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251267779.

records.title: Module-specific diagnostic accuracy of ADOS-2 in real-world clinical referral populations: an updated systematic review and HSROC meta-analysis.

content.title: Module-specific diagnostic accuracy of ADOS-2 in real-world clinical referral populations: an updated systematic review and HSROC meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

The Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule, Second Edition (ADOS-2), is widely used in the diagnostic evaluation of autism spectrum disorder (ASD); however, its diagnostic performance in real-world clinical referral populations remains heterogeneous, particularly across modules and clinical contexts. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the module-specific diagnostic accuracy of ADOS-2 using hierarchical meta-analytic modeling and examined sources of heterogeneity in updated evidence clinical studies.

Methods

A systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted from January 2021 to February 2026, with additional screening of reference lists. Studies were included if they evaluated ADOS-2 diagnostic accuracy in real-world clinical referral populations, used DSM- or ICD-based clinical best-estimate diagnosis as the reference standard, and reported extractable 2×2 data. Diagnostic accuracy was pooled using a hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) model with a bivariate random-effects approach. Module-specific analyses (Toddler Module, Modules 1-2, Module 3, Module 4) and meta-regression were performed to examine heterogeneity.

Results

Ten studies were included in the qualitative synthesis, and six provided extractable 2×2 data for quantitative pooling. Overall pooled sensitivity was 0.88 (95% CI: 0.83-0.92) and pooled specificity was 0.74 (95% CI: 0.68-0.80), with an HSROC AUC of 0.86. The Toddler Module showed the highest diagnostic performance (sensitivity 0.92; specificity 0.88; AUC 0.94), whereas specificity decreased in Modules 3 and 4. Meta-regression identified module level, psychiatric referral setting, and adult samples as significant contributors to reduced specificity. No significant publication bias was detected.

Conclusions

ADOS-2 demonstrates high overall sensitivity but variable specificity across modules in real-world clinical referral populations. Reduced specificity was more commonly observed in higher ADOS-2 modules, which are typically administered to verbally fluent adolescents and adults with greater psychiatric complexity.

records.title: Machine Learning in Palliative Care: Scoping Review of Applications.

content.title: Machine Learning in Palliative Care: Scoping Review of Applications.
content.abstract:
Background

Palliative care is increasingly recognized as essential for an aging population and rising life-limiting illnesses. Machine learning (ML) has been widely applied in this field, primarily for prognostication. However, recent literature suggests broader applications that may enhance patient-centered care and optimize system-level processes.

Objective

This study aimed to map and summarize the evolving landscape of ML applications in palliative care through a scoping review, identifying how studies extend beyond mortality prediction into new domains, while assessing explainability, equity, and implementation readiness.

Methods

We conducted a scoping review following the Arksey and O'Malley framework and PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) guidelines. Six databases (MEDLINE, PsycINFO, Embase, CINAHL, Scopus, and Web of Science) were searched from inception to April 15, 2021, with an update through February 9, 2026. Included studies were peer-reviewed primary studies applying ML to palliative care contexts. Each study was coded for explainable AI (XAI) methods, equity considerations, and implementation readiness. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data. Synthesis combined descriptive statistics and inductive thematic analysis. Consistent with scoping review methodology, no formal risk-of-bias assessment was performed.

Results

We included 121 studies (2015-2026) spanning 24 countries, with 69.4% (84/121) published from 2021 onward. The United States contributed the largest share (66/121, 54.5%), followed by Japan, Taiwan, and China (22/121, 18.2%). Cancer was the most commonly studied population (52/121, 43%). Supervised classification was the most common approach (84/121, 69.4%), followed by natural language processing and text mining (16/121, 13.2%). Six application domains were identified: mortality and survival prediction (51/121, 42.1%), health care use (25/121, 20.7%), symptom assessment and phenotyping (20/121, 16.5%), communication and natural language processing (16/121, 13.2%), clinical decision support and care quality (6/121, 5%), and other (3/121, 2.5%). Approximately half of the studies (61/121, 50.4%) used at least one XAI technique, most commonly feature importance rankings and SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) values. Among the 121 studies, equity in model performance was fully addressed in only 8 (6.6%) studies, partially in 8 (6.6%) studies, and not addressed in 105 (86.8%) studies. Two-thirds of studies (80/121, 66.1%) remained at the proof-of-concept stage, while 16.5% (20/121) achieved external validation and 17.4% (21/121) reached prospective deployment or clinical integration.

Conclusions

ML applications in palliative care are expanding beyond prognostication toward patient-centered uses, including symptom management, clinical decision support, and resource planning. The persistent gap in equity reporting (105/121, 86.8% did not report equity considerations) signals that the field risks developing tools that may not perform equitably across diverse populations. While half of studies now use XAI techniques, fewer than 1 in 5 studies (21/121, 17.4%) have reached clinical integration. Bridging this translational gap requires systematic attention to implementation science, equity auditing, and explainability reporting.

records.title: Artificial intelligence for lung cancer: a systematic review of head‑to‑head CT, FDG PET/CT, and multimodal models across screening, staging, and prognosis.

content.title: Artificial intelligence for lung cancer: a systematic review of head‑to‑head CT, FDG PET/CT, and multimodal models across screening, staging, and prognosis.
content.abstract:
Background

Artificial intelligence (AI) has shown increasing potential in lung cancer imaging, particularly in detection, staging, prognosis, and recurrence prediction. However, there is limited synthesis of head-to-head comparative evidence between CT, FDG PET/CT, and multimodal fusion models within the same cohorts.

Objectives

To systematically review and critically appraise studies that directly compared CT-only, FDG PET/CT-only, and combined multimodal models in lung cancer, with emphasis on clinical setting, fusion strategy, validation design, and clinical utility.

Methods

This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-S guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar were searched for English-language human studies published between January 1, 2019, and September 8, 2025. Eligible studies reported same-cohort, head-to-head comparisons of CT, PET/CT, or multimodal models for lung cancer screening, staging, or prognosis. Risk of bias was assessed using PROBAST for prediction model studies and SANRA for narrative reviews. Data were extracted in duplicate and synthesized narratively, with meta-analysis performed where ≥ 3 studies were sufficiently homogeneous.

Results

From 2,417 records (PubMed 845, Scopus 920, IEEE Xplore 452, Google Scholar/manual 200), 31 studies met inclusion criteria (20 primary modeling studies, 11 reviews). In screening cohorts, low-dose CT deep-learning models consistently outperformed other modalities, with modest incremental value from clinical covariates. For nodal staging, integrated PET/CT radiomics-clinical models showed superior discrimination, calibration, and net-benefit compared with unimodal approaches. In prognostic and recurrence settings, fused PET/CT models outperformed CT- or PET-only models across institutions, with further improvement from clinical variables. Radiogenomics and pathology integration provided added value but were limited by small samples and lack of external validation.

Conclusions

Comparative evidence demonstrates that modality performance is context-dependent: CT dominates in screening, PET/CT fusion excels in staging and prognosis, and multimodal integration with clinical or biomarker data enhances discrimination and utility. Standardization, harmonization, and rigorous external validation remain critical for generalizability.

Clinical trial number

Not applicable.

records.title: Virtual reality for reducing pain, anxiety, and distress in children, adolescents, and young adults with cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

content.title: Virtual reality for reducing pain, anxiety, and distress in children, adolescents, and young adults with cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
content.abstract:
Background

Needle-related procedures are a significant source of pain, anxiety, and distress for children with cancer. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of virtual reality (VR) as a distraction intervention for reducing these outcomes in pediatric oncology patients undergoing needle-related procedures.

Methods

A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, PsycINFO, and CINAHL was conducted from database inception to March 23, 2026. We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating the effect of VR (immersive or non-immersive) compared to standard care or active distraction in pediatric oncology patients (aged ≤21 years) undergoing needle-related procedures. The primary outcome was self-reported pain.
